environment.description: Same EC2 instance (m5.large, Amazon Linux 2) but the application runs inside a Docker container with the following runtime constraints: rootfs mounted read-only (--read-only flag), no tmpfs volumes mounted (no --tmpfs flags), /app/keys volume mounted from host with file permissions 0600 owned by root (container runs as uid 1000). The container's seccomp profile is set to the default Docker profile. An NLB forwards traffic on port 443 with TLS termination. The container has no capability to read /app/keys/public.pem due to file ownership mismatch (root:root 0600, process runs as appuser:1000). Without access to the public key material, the HS256 algorithm confusion attack cannot be performed because the attacker cannot obtain the key bytes needed to forge the HMAC signature.
